<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917575_theRebbe_481" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917575_theRebbe_481__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the proof from the obligation for a husband to visit his wife before a journey shows that the unification (Pekidah) occurred even during the time of the Temple's pledging, as seen in the cherubim embracing during the destruction.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="2">that this which [the Alter Rebbe] brings in Likkutei Torah as a proof that the unification is called "Pekidah" from that which our sages of blessed memory said, "A man is obligated to visit his wife,"</t>
    <t s="3">is,</t>
    <t s="4">because this statement of our sages of blessed memory speaks of the obligation to visit his wife at the time when he is going out on a journey,</t>
    <t s="5">and in this it hints,</t>
    <t s="6">that in addition to the matter of the "Pekudei HaMishkan" (the accountings of the Tabernacle),</t>
    <t s="7">that the intention in this—that the Sanctuary was pledged—is in order that through repentance there will be afterward</t>
    <t s="8">(in the future to come)</t>
    <t s="9">the unification</t>
    <t s="10">(Pekidah)</t>
    <t s="11">in a more elevated manner,</t>
    <t s="12">even during this very time itself</t>
    <t s="13">(when the Sanctuary was pledged)</t>
    <t s="14">there was the unification.</t>
    <t s="15">And as is explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="16">what our sages of blessed memory said,</t>
    <t s="17">"At the time when the gentiles entered the Sanctuary, they saw the cherubim intertwined with each other,"</t>
    <t s="18">for this is seemingly perplexing,</t>
    <t s="19">for cherubim intertwined with each other indicates the greatness of the affection of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel, like the affection of a man and a woman,</t>
    <t s="20">and at the time when the gentiles entered the Sanctuary, it was seemingly the opposite of affection.</t>
    <t s="21">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="22">that since during the time of exile the Congregation of Israel is like a woman whose husband has gone to a country overseas,</t>
    <t s="23">therefore,</t>
    <t s="24">before the departure of the husband</t>
    <t s="25">(the Holy One, blessed be He)</t>
    <t s="26">on the journey,</t>
    <t s="27">there was the "Pekidah" (visitation/unification),</t>
    <t s="28">and therefore the cherubim were then like the embracing</t>
    <t s="29">of a man and his wife.</t>
    <t s="30">However, the Pekidah that took place then was in concealment,</t>
    <t s="31">and in revelation there was the destruction and the exile,</t>
    <t s="32">and the intention in this is that through the service during the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="33">and particularly through the service of repentance,</t>
    <t s="34">the Pekidah will be revealed in the building of the Third Holy Temple,</t>
    <t s="35">and then the pledge will also be returned,</t>
    <t s="36">the Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony,</t>
    <t s="37">with the coming of Mashiach Tzidkeinu, speedily and truly.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
